never: Never resolves a piece with a redemptive moral or a lesson tidily learned.
Never uses intensifiers like 'very,' 'really,' or 'incredibly' to carry emotion.
Never tells the reader how to feel; she places the facts and withdraws.
Never makes a joke or winks; irony comes only from juxtaposition.
Never floats in the abstract without grounding it in a specific place, date, or object.
Never uses the first person as confession or plea for sympathy.
Never trusts the consoling shape of narrative or lets a story close cleanly.
Never pads with adverbs where a placed noun would do the work.
always: Always anchors the scene in exact particulars: dates, brand names, highway numbers, temperatures.
Always keeps the prose cool even when the subject is catastrophe.
Always builds long accumulating sentences that end on a short clipped clause.
Always uses repetition of phrase and image as structural ballast.
Always asserts authority through what the first-person observer notices.
Always reaches for the rhetorical hinge ('I tell you this because,' 'I am talking here about').
Always lets the piece end on an unresolved, slightly ominous note.
Always trusts the reader to feel the dread without being instructed to.
